name: Montréal
coordsNote: Downtown/Plateau edge; the long-stay areas are Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mile End just north.

english.rationale: Canada is not ranked by EF EPI (English is an official language). Montréal is French-majority, but Statistics Canada reports 69% of Montréal-CMA workers are English-French bilingual and 21% work mainly in English; in the Plateau, Mile End and downtown, service in English is routine. Signage and some official interactions are French-first under Quebec law.

sources.title: Statistics Canada: Languages at work, spotlight on Montréal
sources.quote: Among workers in the Montréal census metropolitan area (CMA), 80% were at least bilingual (69% English–French bilingual)

vibe: Bilingual festival city: Plateau walk-ups, bagels and terrasses; severe winters
narrative: A French-speaking city with European-style neighbourhoods: Plateau and Mile End walk-ups with outdoor staircases, wood-fired bagels, Mount Royal's park above downtown, and a summer run of free outdoor shows from the Jazz Fest through Just for Laughs and Osheaga. Winters are severe, with months of snow and deep-freeze cold, so it works best as a June-to-September base.

season.rationale: Editorial estimate. Visitor demand and short-stay prices concentrate in the festival summer (Grand Prix late May, then the Jazz Fest, Just for Laughs and Osheaga from late June to early August); September-October stay busy with mild weather and fall colour. November to April is the low season despite winter festivals (Igloofest, Montréal en Lumière); late March-April is thaw/slush season. December gets some holiday travel.

safety.propertyNote: Safe overall; petty theft and car break-ins in busy areas
safety.womensSafetyNote: Busy, walkable central neighbourhoods; ordinary night-time caution
safety.touristRationale: Crimes against visitors are mostly opportunistic theft; no visitor-specific pattern beyond that.

rationale.property: The State Dept describes Canadian crime against foreigners as crimes of opportunity (pickpocketing, purse snatching, car break-ins), common in tourist areas. Set slightly above Vancouver (72), whose downtown has more visible open-air disorder; below Taipei/Tokyo-tier cities.
rationale.tourist: No evidence that visitors are targeted beyond opportunistic theft; Level 1 advisory. 1.0, as for Vancouver.
rationale.womens: +10 on Canada's Gallup baseline, one point under Vancouver (+11): dense, busy central neighbourhoods with late-running metro; no Montréal-specific survey found, so kept close to the calibrated comparator.

selection: North America has one city today; Montréal's festival summer (Jazz Fest, Just for Laughs, Osheaga) and European-style neighbourhoods make it a strong June-September base on the continent. Winters are severe.
researchNotes: Advisory: travel.state.gov returned a Cloudflare bot challenge (not bypassed); level/text read from cadataapi.state.gov (Published 2026-06-04T20:00-04:00 = 2026-06-05 UTC; the API's Japan entry maps the same way onto its RSS date). Hazards left empty: wildfire smoke reached Montréal in some recent summers (e.g. 2023) but it is episodic rather than seasonal, matching Vancouver's treatment; extreme winter cold is not a hazard class here and is handled by the climate pipeline. homicideOverride null (country baseline). Quebec restricts short-term rentals, so furnished stays are typically 31-night minimum.
